These are individual private schools running executive or rolling-entry cohorts, not national admission cycles. No public university in France admits in those months. If you are planning your year around a March intake, you are planning around something that does not exist at scale. Both France intakes lead to the same degree and the same [post-study options in France](https://leapscholar.com/blog/study-in-france-for-indian-students/). The difference is programme choice, funding access, and how your Indian academic calendar lines up. ***Counselor insight:*** *Roughly 70% of Indian students in France are enrolled in management master's programs, with engineering next at about 11%, according to Campus France India's national coordinator in an interview with*[*Careers360*](https://news.careers360.com/study-abroad-campus-france-india-margo-girard-application-process-fee-higher-education)*. That distribution matters for intake choice: management is exactly the field where January cohorts are most common, so business applicants have a genuine second window that engineering applicants largely do not.* ## **September vs January France Intakes: Which Window Fits Your Timeline?** The September intake wins for most Indian applicants. The comparison below shows why, and where January still makes sense. | **Factor** | **September 2027 intake** | **January 2028 intake** | | --- | --- | --- | | Application window | Approx. 1 Oct to 15 Dec 2026 (DAP route) | Approx. Sep to Nov 2027 | | Classes begin | Mid to late September 2027 | January 2028 | | Programme availability | All levels, all institution types | Business schools, selected master's | | Public universities | Yes, this is their only cycle | Rarely | | Scholarship access | Charpak, Eiffel, institutional aid all aligned here | Significantly thinner | | Competition | Higher volume of applicants | Lower volume, fewer seats | | Internship (*stage*) cycle | In step with French recruitment calendar | Out of step by one semester | | Visa queue | Long, peaks June to August | Shorter, less congested | | Best suited to | Students whose results and documents land on time | Students whose results slipped, or business applicants adding a second attempt | The honest downside of January: you enter the *stage* cycle half a year out of sync. French companies recruit interns on a September-anchored calendar, and a January starter often reaches their internship search when the good positions have already been filled by the September cohort. ***Counselor insight:*** *The January intake is genuinely right for one profile, which is the student whose final semester results or degree certificate arrive too late for a December deadline. For everyone else it is a compromise. Both the Charpak and Eiffel calendars are built around a September start, so a January applicant is usually choosing to skip a funding cycle worth up to Rs.94,000 per month in stipend.* ## **September 2027 France Intake: Confirmed and Expected Deadlines** Here is the part no other guide will tell you plainly. **The 2027-28 calendar has not been published yet.** Campus France's procedure page, last updated 20 November 2025, still carries only the 2026-2027 dates. That is not a reason to wait. The DAP window has opened on 1 October and closed on 15 December for consecutive cycles. Plan on that pattern and confirm the exact dates when they appear on the portal. | **Stage** | **2026-27 published date** | **2027-28 status** | | --- | --- | --- | | DAP registrations open | 1 October 2025 | Expect approx. 1 October 2026 | | DAP registrations close | 15 December 2025 | Expect approx. 15 December 2026 | | University decisions | Before 30 April 2026 | Expect approx. April 2027 | | Your reply to offers | Before 31 May 2026 | Expect approx. May 2027 | | Classes begin | September 2026 | September 2027 | Source for all 2026-27 dates: [Campus France, Études en France procedure](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/application-etudes-en-france-procedure). Two things Indian applicants get wrong here: 1. **No answer counts as a refusal.** If you receive offers and do not reply by the stated date, the silence is treated as a rejection. This is written into the procedure. 2. **Parcoursup is not your platform.** Parcoursup opened 17 December 2025 for the 2026-27 cycle, but it applies to students preparing a French or European Baccalauréat. If you are a CBSE, ICSE or state board student, your route is DAP through Études en France. ***Counselor insight:*** *The files that clear fastest are opened in the first two weeks of October. Campus France India operates through offices in a limited number of cities, and interview slots compress badly in the second half of the window. A student who submits on 12 December is competing for an appointment against everyone else who waited, in the same three weeks, at the same handful of centres.* ## **January 2028 France Intake: Who It Actually Suits** The January intake in France opens roughly September to November 2027 and runs at a much smaller set of institutions. Realistically available program types: * MBA and Master in Management at private business schools * Selected MSc programmes in finance, marketing and international business * A small number of specialised engineering and data master's at private schools Two cautions before you build a plan around it: * **Verify the cohort actually runs.** School websites list January starts that have not run for two admission cycles. Ask the admissions office in writing whether the January 2028 cohort is confirmed and how many seats it holds. * **Scholarship access is thinner.** Charpak and Eiffel calls are anchored to September. Institutional aid for January cohorts is smaller and awarded to fewer students. You will still need the full Campus France process, the same [English proficiency scores](https://leapscholar.com/exams/ielts), and the same proof of funds. January is a different date, not a lighter process. ***Counselor insight:*** *Ask one specific question when you contact a January programme: how many students started in the last January cohort? A cohort of 12 against a September cohort of 90 tells you what your peer network, alumni access and campus recruitment will look like for two years.* ## **How to Apply Through Campus France for Both France Intakes** Indian nationals must apply through the Études en France (EEF) platform. This is not an alternative to applying directly to a university. It is a prerequisite for your student visa, and India is one of 73 countries and territories covered by the procedure, per [Campus France](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/application-etudes-en-france-procedure). The eight steps, in order: 1. **Create your EEF account** on the Études en France platform. 2. **Build your academic profile:** every year of schooling, every marksheet, no gaps. 3. **Upload documents,** translated into French or English where required. 4. **Select programs:** up to 3 under DAP, or up to 7 under the Hors DAP route for Master 1 and Master 2 or Licence 2 and 3. 5. **Pay the EEF procedure fee** of Rs.20,000, increased from Rs.18,500 on 1 August 2026 per Campus France India.. 6. **Attend the Campus France interview** at your nearest centre. 7. **Receive the pre-consular opinion,** then complete biometrics at VFS Global. 8. **Apply for the VLS-TS long-stay visa** and validate it within three months of arriving in France. Private schools and some Grandes Écoles run their own admission round in parallel. You still route through Campus France for the visa. ***Counselor insight:*** *A program list spread across unrelated fields is the most common self-inflicted wound in an Indian file. A shortlist containing a master's in marketing alongside one in mechanical engineering reads as an incoherent study plan at the interview stage. Pick a lane, then vary by institution and city, not by discipline.* ## **What the 2027-28 France Intakes Will Cost Indian Students** Three cost rules changed in 2026. All three land on the 2027-28 cohort. ### **Tuition at public universities** | **Programme** | **Non-EU rate** | **EU rate for comparison** | | --- | --- | --- | | Bachelor's (Licence) | Rs.3,18,320 (€2,902) | Rs.19,525 (€178) | | Master's | Rs.4,33,276 (€3,950) | Rs.27,971 (€255) | | Doctorate (PhD) | Rs.43,657 (€398) | Rs.43,547 (€397) | Source: [Campus France, Tuition fees in France](https://www.campusfrance.org/en/tuition-fees-France), updated 25 June 2026, 2026-27 rates. PhD programmes are not subject to differentiated fees. Private institutions and business schools set their own fees, generally Rs.6.58 lakh to Rs.19.74 lakh (€6,000 to €18,000) or more per year, per the same Campus France page. ### **The exemption change that matters most for 2027-28** Until recently, most non-EU students at French public universities were exempted from the higher rate. That is ending on a published schedule. Under [Decree No. 2026-385 of 19 May 2026](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000054113646), each institution may exempt only a capped share of its non-EU students per category: | **Academic year** | **Exemption cap** | | --- | --- | | 2026-27 | 30% | | **2027-28** | **25%** | | 2028-29 onward | 20% | Confirmed on the French Ministry of Higher Education's [FAQ on differentiated fees](https://www.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/fr/faq-droits-d-inscription-differencies-pour-les-etudiants-extra-communautaires-101557) and [Service-Public.gouv.fr](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/actualites/A18927?lang=en). If you are applying for 2027-28, budget for the full rate and treat a waiver as a bonus. ### **Mandatory fees and living costs** | **Item** | **Amount** | **Note** | | --- | --- | --- | | CVEC (student life contribution) | Rs.11,517 (€105) | Fixed for 2026-27 per [Service-Public](https://www.service-public.gouv.fr/particuliers/vosdroits/F36520/2). Paid once per year | | Proof of funds, monthly | Rs.96,254 (€877.50) | From 1 August 2026 | | Proof of funds, annual | Rs.11,55,037 (€10,530) | What your bank statements must support | | EEF procedure fee | *-* | Confirm with Campus France India | | Visa and VLS-TS validation | *-* | Published figures conflict. Confirm on france-visas.gouv.fr | *Exchange rate used: Rs.109.69 per EUR. Verify the current rate before finalising your budget.* ### **The proof-of-funds increase, in plain numbers** [Campus France India confirmed on 24 July 2026](https://www.inde.campusfrance.org/france-visa-important-announcement) that from **1 August 2026**, the minimum financial resources for a French student visa rose to €877.50 per month, replacing €615. | **Old threshold** | **New threshold** | **Difference** | | --- | --- | --- | | Per month | Rs.67,459 (€615) | Rs.96,254 (€877.50) | Rs.28,795 | | Per year | Rs.8,09,512 (€7,380) | Rs.11,55,037 (€10,530) | **Rs.3,45,525** | Most guides still ranking for this topic show the €615 figure. If you built your loan sanction or bank balance around it, you are Rs.3.46 lakh short before tuition. ### **One more cost most guides have not caught** From 1 July 2026, non-EU students who do not hold a scholarship are no longer eligible for APL housing benefit, under the 2026 finance law upheld by the Conseil constitutionnel. Those payments were worth roughly €150 to €250 per month, which is Rs.16,454 to Rs.27,423 a month gone from a typical Indian student's budget. ***Counselor insight:*** *Stack the three 2026 changes and a self-funded Indian master's applicant for 2027-28 is looking at roughly Rs.3.46 lakh more in proof of funds, up to Rs.4.33 lakh in tuition that most students previously had waived, and up to Rs.3.29 lakh a year in lost APL. Families who budgeted from a 2024 or 2025 blog post are short by several lakh, and that gap is what turns an admission letter into an unused admission letter.* *For a full breakdown by city and institution type, see LeapScholar's guide to the*[*cost of studying in France*](https://leapscholar.com/france/cost-of-studying-in-france)*.* ## **Documents Required for the 2027-28 France Intakes** | **Document** | **What Campus France expects** | **India-specific note** | | --- | --- | --- | | Class 10 and 12 certificates | Board certificates and marksheets | CBSE, ICSE and state board certificates all accepted. Include the mark statement, not only the pass certificate | | Bachelor's marksheets | All semesters or all years | Submit consolidated marksheet plus individual semester sheets. Autonomous colleges should add the affiliating university name | | Degree certificate | Final award document | Indian universities often issue this months after results. A provisional certificate on university letterhead with the registrar's seal is normally accepted | | Transcript | Official, sealed | Request early. Many Indian universities take 3 to 6 weeks and charge per copy | | English proficiency | [IELTS](https://leapscholar.com/exams/ielts), [TOEFL](https://leapscholar.com/exams/toefl) or equivalent, per programme | Book your test with buffer. [Practice tests](https://leapscholar.com/exams/ielts/practice-test) before booking help you avoid a costly retake | | French proficiency | DELF or DALF where required | Mandatory at B2 for French-taught programs and for ENSA architecture regardless of teaching language. | | GMAT or GRE | Program-dependent | Common for MBA and MiM at business schools. Not standard for public university master's. See [GMAT preparation](https://leapscholar.com/exams/gmat/preparation) | | [Statement of Purpose](https://leapscholar.com/blog/statement-of-purpose-format-and-meaning/) | Motivation for the program, institution and France | Must survive the Campus France interview. Do not write anything you cannot defend aloud | | [Letters of Recommendation](https://leapscholar.com/blog/letter-of-recommendation/) | Usually two | Indian faculty often need 3 to 4 weeks and a reminder. Request before your final semester ends | | Passport | First page, valid | Apply now if you do not hold one. Passport Seva appointment plus issue can take 4 to 8 weeks | | Proof of funds | Bank statements, loan sanction, sponsor affidavit | Must support Rs.96,254 (€877.50) per month. Last 3 months of statements, in your name or your sponsor's | | CV | Two pages | Reverse chronological. Include internships and projects with dates | ***Counselor insight:*** *The document that stalls Indian files most often is the degree certificate, because the DAP window closes in December 2026 while a final-year student's degree will not exist until mid-2027. This is not a problem you solve by waiting. Confirm in writing this month what your university's provisional certificate looks like and how fast it is issued, because that single piece of paper decides whether September 2027 is realistic for you.* ## **Month-by-Month Plan for the September 2027 France Intake** Mapped to the Indian academic year. | **When** | **What you do** | | --- | --- | | **Aug to Sep 2026** | Shortlist 6 to 10 programmes in one discipline. Book IELTS or TOEFL. Apply for a passport if you do not have one. Request transcripts. | | **Sep 2026** | Sit your English test. Ask two referees for LORs. Check each shortlisted institution's own deadline, which may fall before the DAP close. | | **Nov to Dec 2026** | Pay the EEF fee. Submit. Book your Campus France interview early. | | **Dec 2026 to Feb 2027** | Attend the interview. Keep your bank trail clean and stable. Apply for Charpak when the 2027 call opens. | | **Mar to Apr 2027** | University responses arrive. Complete visa application and VFS biometrics. | | **Jul to Aug 2027** | Visa decision. Arrange accommodation. Pay CVEC. Book flights. | | **Sep 2027** | Arrive, complete enrolment, validate your VLS-TS within three months. | Scholarship timing to watch: Eiffel nominations run through the institution, not the student, and typically open around October for the following September. Charpak calls for 2027 are not yet published. Both are listed on the [Campus France India scholarships page](https://www.inde.campusfrance.org/scholarships-for-indian-students). LeapScholar's overview of [scholarships in France](https://leapscholar.com/france/scholarships-in-france) covers eligibility in more detail. ***Counselor insight:*** *The awkward truth in this calendar is the seven-month gap. The DAP window closes in December 2026, and a final-year Indian student will not hold a degree certificate until roughly July 2027. Every applicant in that position is admitted on provisional documents. Students who discover this in November, after the window has opened, lose weeks they did not need to lose.* ## **Which France Intake Should You Choose? Three Scenarios** **If you are a final-year BTech student graduating in May 2027:** target September 2027. Open your EEF file in October 2026 using your first six or seven semester marksheets. You will submit a provisional certificate in June or July 2027. Confirm now that your college issues one within two weeks of results, because if it takes six weeks you will miss the visa queue and January 2028 becomes your realistic intake. **If you are a Class 12 CBSE student appearing for boards in March 2027:** September 2027 is tight and September 2028 may serve you better. The DAP window closes in December 2026, before your boards. If you are applying for 2027 entry, you will be assessed largely on Class 11 and predicted performance, and your bachelor's tuition will be Rs.3.18 lakh (€2,902) a year with only a 25% exemption pool. Consider a gap-free alternative: apply in the October 2027 window for September 2028, with final board marks in hand. **If you are a working professional with 3 years of experience targeting an MBA or MiM:** both France intakes are open to you, and January 2028 is a real option because business schools run it. Weigh two things. First, your notice period against a January start that leaves little room for delay. Second, cost: private school fees of Rs.6.58 lakh to Rs.19.74 lakh (€6,000 to €18,000) plus Rs.11.55 lakh in proof of funds, against September's fuller scholarship access. If funding matters more than starting six months sooner, choose September. ***Counselor insight:*** *The deciding variable is almost never preference. It is whether your documents will physically exist by the deadline. Two students with identical profiles end up in different France intakes because one university issues provisional certificates in ten days and the other takes two months.* ## **What to Do If Your France Intake Application Goes Wrong** | **Problem** | **What to do** | | --- | --- | | **Missed the December DAP close** | Pivot to January 2028 at a private school, or use the extra year to strengthen your profile for September 2028. Do not submit a rushed incomplete file. | | **Degree certificate delayed past the deadline** | Submit the provisional certificate with a covering letter from your registrar stating the expected issue date. Flag it to your Campus France manager rather than leaving a gap in the file. | | **IELTS or DELF score below the requirement** | Retake if there is time. Some programmes accept a conditional offer pending a resit. Check whether the institution accepts an alternative test before paying for the same one twice. | | **Campus France interview goes badly** | You will usually receive a reasoned pre-consular opinion. Address the specific weakness identified, whether that is study-plan coherence or funding, before reapplying. Do not reapply with the same answers. | | **Proof of funds short of Rs.96,254 per month** | Do not top up with a sudden large transfer. Unexplained lump sums weaken a file more than a modest balance does. Use a sanctioned education loan or a documented sponsor with a clean statement history. | | **Visa refused** | Request the reason. Financial refusals are often recoverable in the next cycle once the money trail is rebuilt properly over three months. Reapplying with the same statements turns one refusal into two. | ***Counselor insight:*** *Insufficient or poorly documented funds is a more common cause of a weak French student visa file than low marks or a low English score. With the threshold now at Rs.11.55 lakh (€10,530) for the year and APL no longer available to most Indian students, the financial section of your file deserves more preparation time than your SOP.* ## **3 Takeaways on France Intakes** 1. **Open your Études en France file in the first two weeks of October 2026,** not in mid-2027. The DAP window has closed on 15 December for consecutive cycles, and interview slots run out before the deadline does. 2. **Budget on Rs.96,254 (€877.50) a month in proof of funds and the full differentiated tuition rate.** With the 2027-28 exemption pool capped at 25% and APL no longer available to most Indian students, treat any waiver as a bonus rather than an assumption. 3. **Ask your Indian university this week how fast it issues a provisional certificate.** That answer, more than your marks or your test score, decides whether September 2027 or January 2028 is your realistic intake. ***Verified by:*** *LeapScholar's France counseling team, with hands-on experience guiding Indian students through the Campus France Études en France procedure and the VLS-TS long-stay student visa.* *Have questions about the 2027-28 France intakes?* [*Book a free session with a LeapScholar counselor*](https://leapscholar.com/webflow_progressive_form?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=in-content-cta&utm_campaign=counselling)*.* ## **Frequently Asked Questions About France Intakes** * ##### **What are the monthly living expenses for a student in France in rupees?** Plan on at least Rs.96,254 (€877.50) a month, because that is now the visa floor rather than a comfortable estimate. Paris runs higher than Toulouse, Lille or Montpellier. Budget upward from July 2026, when non-EU students without a scholarship stopped being eligible for APL housing benefit worth roughly Rs.16,454 to Rs.27,423 a month. * ##### **What happens if my final-year marksheet arrives after the France intake deadline**? Submit a provisional certificate issued on university letterhead with the registrar's seal, along with a covering letter stating when the final certificate will be released. This is standard for Indian final-year students, since the DAP window closes in December while Indian results arrive around June. Tell your Campus France manager rather than leaving the field blank. * ##### **Are there scholarships available for the January intake in France?** Fewer than for September. The France Excellence Charpak and Eiffel programs are built around a September start, and institutional aid for January cohorts is smaller. If funding is a deciding factor, September is materially stronger. Charpak and Eiffel calls for 2027 have not been published yet, so check the Campus France India scholarships page rather than relying on last year's dates. * ##### **Will I have to pay the higher tuition fees for the 2027-28 France intakes?** Most likely yes. Non-EU rates for 2026-27 are Rs.3,18,320 (€2,902) for a bachelor's and Rs.4,33,276 (€3,950) for a master's. Under Decree No. 2026-385, each institution may exempt only 25% of its non-EU students in 2027-28, down from 30% in 2026-27. Budget for the full rate. * ##### **How much money do I need to show for a France student visa in 2027?** From 1 August 2026, applicants must show a minimum of €877.50 per month, which is Rs.96,254, replacing the earlier €615 threshold. Across twelve months that is Rs.11,55,037 (€10,530), supported by bank statements, a sanctioned education loan, or documented sponsor funds. Most guides still show the old figure, leaving a Rs.3.46 lakh shortfall. * ##### **Can I apply directly to a French university without Campus France?** Indian nationals must complete the Études en France procedure. The Director of Studies will contact you by email with more information. **Beware: the application platforms are different!** Eligibility and requirements **The information given below concerns mainly non-local students, meaning students applying from a foreign university or from a French University other than UGA and Grenoble INP.** AM, AI, MSIAM, MoSIG, CySec, and ORCO are highly competitive academic programs, with selection on the basis of prior academic and/or scientific achievement as documented by academic transcripts, a cover letter, letters of recommendation and standardized test scores. Language requirements Students are required to provide evidence of their proficiency in English. English scores accepted for the MoSIG, AM, MSIAM, CySec and ORCO programs: | Test name | Minimum general score | | --- | --- | | Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) | C | | Cambridge C2 Proficiency (CPE) | C | | IELTS Academic | 6.0 | | Pearson Test of English Academic PTE A | 62 | | TOEFL IBT (Internet-based test) | 78 | | TOEFL ITP (Paper-delivered test) | 547 | | TOEIC 4-Skills | 700 | If you have successfully completed a degree (or equivalent) at a University in one of the following countries then you meet the English requirements automatically: Australia, Canada (except Quebec), Guyana, Ireland, New Zealand, United Kingdom, United States of America, West Indies. This list is exhaustive. **If you live in a country in conflict, get in touch with us at masters-admission@ensimag.fr to know which rule applies for you.** **No other exceptions will be made to those prerequisites and the documents requested.** **No application will be reviewed without having met those requirements.** **Please note that even if your test is outdated we will consider it as valid.** Degree requirements For admission to the full two-year program you must have a Bachelor's Degree of at least 3 years duration (equivalent to the European Licence). **The minimum requirement is to have earned at least the equivalent of 180 ECTS credits** For admission directly to the second year of the program (MSIAM-M2, MoSIG-M2, AI-M2, CySec or ORCO) you must have a 4-year Bachelor's Degree or equivalent, or be currently enrolled in master's studies. **The minimum requirement is to have earned at least the equivalent of 240 ECTS credits**. MoSIG (M1 - M2) To be admitted to the program, candidates must have previously completed their undergraduate studies and been awarded a Bachelor degree in either Science (BSc) or Engineering (BEng) that includes courses in computing and solid practice in programming. Applications of candidates with bachelor in Computer Science or Computer Engineering will be preferably considered. Skills in mathematics (algebra, probability theory) and Informatics (C/C++/JAVA, algorithms, Computer architectures, Operating Systems principles), Data bases and software engineering are required. AI (M1 - M2) To be admitted to the programme, candidates must hold either a Bachelor of at least 3 years duration (for the M1) or a first year of master with 60 ECTS credits (for the M2) in computer science, computer engineering, mathematics or applied mathematics or an equivalent degree. Candidates must be: * Interested in pursuing advanced education in artificial intelligence * Proficient in mathematics (algebra, probability theory, arithmetic) and programming. Entrance tests on prerequisite mathematics and programming may be required. AM (M1) To be admitted to the program, candidates must have previously completed their undergraduate studies and been awarded a Bachelor degree in Mathematics or Applied Mathematics. Who can apply? * Anyone holding a L3 or Bachelor Degree in mathematics or applied mathematics or an equivalent degree, interested in pursuing a high level mathematical education and motivated by the applications of mathematics. * Students from related backgrounds (physics, computer science, engineering, etc) may also apply provided they possess outstanding mathematical qualifications and are highly motivated by applications. MSIAM (M2) To be admitted to the program, candidates must have previously completed their undergraduate studies and been awarded a Bachelor degree in Mathematics or Applied Mathematics. Who can apply? * Anyone holding a first year of master 60ECTS credits in mathematics or applied mathematics or an equivalent degree, interested in pursuing a high level mathematical education and motivated by the applications of mathematics. * Students from related backgrounds (physics, computer science, engineering, etc) may also apply provided they possess outstanding mathematical qualifications and are highly motivated by applications. CySec (M2) To be admitted to the program, candidates shall have previously completed their undergraduate studies and been awarded a Bachelor degree in either Science (BSc) or Engineering (BEng) that includes courses in computing and solid practice in programming. Applications of candidates with bachelor in Computer Science or Computer Engineering will be preferably considered. Skills in mathematics (algebra, probability theory, arithmetics) are required for the optional courses on advanced cryptology. Admission of students is always at the discretion of the Master team which may require that the student attend pre training courses. Who can apply? * Anyone holding a first year of master with 60 ECTS credits in computer science, computer engineering, mathematics or applied mathematics or an equivalent degree; and interested in pursuing a high level education in computer security and cryptology. * Admission is also possible for students having successfully completed the MoSIG-M1 (first year of MoSIG) program including the elective course Introduction to Cryptology and Coding. ORCO (M2) To be admitted to the program, candidates shall have previously completed the first year of a master program (M1) in Computer science, Applied Mathematics or Industrial Engineering, or shall hold an equivalent degree. Basic skills in the following domains would largely be appreciated: probability theory, graph theory, linear programming, branch and bound. Candidates can contact the persons in charge of the master program to have references of books and/or articles on these domains to prepare at best. Instructions for completing the online application process If you encounter difficulties or requests for information that you can not provide, please contact us at * [mosig AT ensimag DOT fr](mailto:mosig@ensimag.fr) * [masterai AT ensimag DOT fr](mailto:masterai@ensimag.fr;) * [msiam AT ensimag DOT fr](mailto:msiam@ensimag.fr) * [m2cybersec AT ensimag DOT fr](mailto:m2cybersec@ensimag.fr) * [orco AT ensimag DOT fr](mailto:orco@ensimag.fr) Students need to apply at least 5 days before the admission committee in order to have their applications assessed. An application submitted 5 days before an admission committee meeting can still be reviewed later, depending on the number of applications we received between two admission committee meeting date. The reviewing date will be displayed on your application summary as soon as it has been flagged as valid to be submitted to our admission committee. Application requires uploading some documents (**either in French or in English**): * Copy of your most recent diplomas, with a translation of the diploma in French or English. * Certified copy of the final grades obtained for all University Studies. * Copy of grades obtained so far for this academic year, and date by which you can provide your final grades (final transcripts will be needed for admission). * Recommendation letter(s). You can submit up to three recommendation letters (print on letter head, and submit using the on-line tool (uploads)). * Certification of competence in French and or English. For application to a program taught in English, a CECR level of B2 (advanced intermediate) is generally required. Test scores and type accepted are detailed on the dedicated section above. Optional documents: * Official description of the grading system in use at your current university * Description of your most recent academic program, including number hours, credits and subjects studied for each class.
